answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each agent to stake a small refundable deposit and build a verifiable work history before it can transact at full limits. Like a river that only grows strong from many tributaries over time, reputation must accumulate gradually through attested tasks, not appear overnight. A whisper of activity from a brand-new identity should earn only tiny limits, while the wider ocean of peers cross-checks behavior and slashes deposits when fraud is proven, making a thousand fake identities cost a thousand stakes plus months of wasted computation.
